summary: Independent review of the reconciliation scope and fill-balance checkpoint fix, which closes the 221-CRITICAL-per-run storm I root-caused this morning. Context I must state plainly: the storm was caused by #961, which I reviewed and PINNED, and it only surfaced because I restarted the reconciler on 09-12 after it had been running 13-day-old code. This PR cleans up a consequence of my own pin. ALL THREE of codex-2's corrections to my write-up were right and mine were wrong. There are SEVEN paper accounts, not six; I wrote six and then listed seven in the same block. The reconciler has NO paging path at all, verified by grepping for ntfy, delivery and page( in reconciliation/service.py and services/reconciler.py and finding nothing, so these findings polluted the DASHBOARD and never phone-paged; my "raising CRITICAL every ~30s" framing implied alerting pressure that does not exist. And an empty strategy_codes means UNATTRIBUTED rather than external, which this PR answers properly by populating it from fill strategies instead of leaving me to infer ownership from its absence. The checkpoint choice is the part I scrutinised hardest and I endorse it. reconciliation_fill_balance_since = 2026-09-12 21:17:49 UTC is anchored to a durable, independently captured flat state: I verified it against oms-recon-restart-before-20260912.json on the box, whose captured_at_utc is 2026-09-12T21:17:49.833386+00:00 and whose live_exposure block records accounts_found 2/2, open_managed_rows 0, nonzero_account_position_rows 0. The shipped constant truncates the sub-second, making it 0.83s EARLIER than the snapshot, which is the safe direction because it can only include more history and never miss a fill. Preferring a fixed verified checkpoint over a rolling age bound is the right call and better than the recency bound I proposed: a rolling window can age a legitimately held position out of evidence, a silent false clean, whereas a fixed checkpoint cannot. test_shipped_fill_balance_checkpoint_is_the_verified_flat_restart pins the exact value so it cannot drift silently. Mutation matrix, 6 mutations, all RED: pushing the checkpoint to 2030 so everything is suppressed turned 8 tests red; dropping the live scope filter red; dropping only is_active red; removing the checkpoint bound from the fill query red; forcing the silent empty return red across 13 tests; and dropping the fill-strategy attribution from strategy_codes red. Production projection verified independently against the database rather than taken from the PR: under the new scope, live and active accounts with fills at or after the checkpoint, ZERO symbols carry a non-zero fill balance, so the 221 stale findings go to zero. I must qualify that number rather than quote it flat: there have been ZERO fills on either live account since the checkpoint, so production data proves only the SUPPRESSION half. The PRESERVATION half, that a genuinely new live mismatch still raises critical, is not demonstrable from production today and rests entirely on the tests, which do cover it via test_post_checkpoint_negative_live_fill_balance_remains_critical and test_pre_checkpoint_history_cannot_hide_a_current_managed_position. Controlled pair, full unit suite, sorted failure-NAME sets: base f6c3d5fb 46 failed / 3782 passed, head 0ecf7e5a 46 failed / 3788 passed, identical 46 names, zero new failures, and the +6 delta is exactly the six new test functions, so the numbers reconcile without residue. Both worktrees asserted to import their own project_mai_tai before any count was trusted. Base is an ancestor of head. OPERATIONAL FINDING FOR THE DEPLOY, not a defect in this PR and not previously flagged by either agent: deploy_preflight.py line 156 appends to failures when critical_findings is greater than zero, so the 221 stale findings currently BLOCK deploy preflight. The fix only takes effect once the reconciler process restarts. Tonight's order must therefore be sync the checkout, RESTART THE RECONCILER FIRST so the findings drop to zero, then run preflight and proceed. Restarting the reconciler last means preflight refuses on findings the sync has already fixed on disk. MINOR OBSERVATION, not blocking: the guard that returns an empty finding list when there are no live account ids means that if the live accounts were ever renamed or deactivated, reconciliation would return no findings and the summary would read as healthy rather than as unmeasured. The tests cannot catch this because they always construct live accounts. Consistent with how this fleet treats UNKNOWN elsewhere, a zero-live-account census would be better reported as unmeasured than as clean. CI: validate passed twice on this head.
